interest: Reveals statutory translations and budgetary data on Japanese shipping subventions compiled for prewar U.S. Maritime Commission policy.
overview: This file comprises State Department records from 1933, 1937, and 1939 documenting Japanese governmental subsidies and financial aid to its merchant marine and shipbuilding industries. It features an extensive 1933 Kobe consular report by Vice Consul Robert M. McClintock analyzing scrap-and-build construction bounties and route subventions alongside international comparisons, accompanied by supervisory commentary and budgetary schedules from Tokyo. The collection also includes 1937 diplomatic despatches and telegrams transmitting official English translations of Japanese subsidy laws and expenditure limits to assist the U.S. Maritime Commission, concluding with a 1939 consular report on operating subventions and subsidized loans granted to major shipping lines Osaka Shosen Kaisha and Nippon Yusen Kaisha.
